financial_summary: Zumiez Inc. is a micro-cap consumer cyclical business with a $222M market cap on $929M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years and +1% annually across the full decade — essentially flat, and Buffett would note that a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 10% cost of capital, which in Buffett’s language means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 35%.

The business throws off $42M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.00× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard Buffett demands so the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 17.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, which is Buffett’s favourite signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 26% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — exactly the alignment Munger looks for, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
